relatednessRule: colors and faker are two package-event records in one related family because independent sources identify a common maintainer and coordinated intentional disruption. They cannot create two independent validation units, and this relationship does not establish a causal mechanism beyond the documented shared-maintainer incident context.

corroboration.snyk: Snyk reports colors@1.4.1 and colors@1.4.44-liberty-2 as intentionally breaking publications and describes faker@6.6.6 as an empty package after a forced repository change by the same maintainer.
corroboration.sonatype: Sonatype independently reports colors 1.4.1, 1.4.2, and 1.4.44-liberty-2 as anomalous and faker@6.6.6 as a functional-code purge, identifying a shared author.
corroboration.russCox: Russ Cox independently documents intentional sabotage of both colors and faker and the contemporaneous impact of a newly published colors version on fresh installs.

strictAdmissionRule.required: Each ledger record requires independently corroborated package/version scope, an official registry timestamp for the earliest assessed affected release, and a retained official registry package-version object strictly before the resulting cutoff.
strictAdmissionRule.result: Both candidate records satisfy the bounded rule. The registry time map sets each strict cutoff; a retained source object exists for the immediate prior retained version selected only by the official time map.

prohibitedInterpretations: The two records are related and count as one future validation unit, not two independent observations.
The selected registry source objects are cutoff-valid source metadata only; they are not package downloads, installs, lockfiles, historical installation trees, or evidence of runtime reach.

Admission does not create controls, benign labels, a complete campaign census, authority features, release comparisons, causal conclusions, scores, models, rankings, calibration, uncertainty intervals, or predictive metrics.
